title: Consecutive upper stupid truncations of module complexes form a short exact sequence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $K$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules with differential of degree $+1$. For $c\in\mathbf Z$, define $\sigma_{\ge c}K$ to agree with $K$ in degrees $i\ge c$ and to be zero in lower degrees, with induced differential. The natural inclusion and projection give a short exact sequence of cochain complexes $0\to\sigma_{\ge c+1}K\to\sigma_{\ge c}K\to K^c[-c]\to0$, where $K^c[-c]$ is the complex with $K^c$ in degree $c$ and zero elsewhere. Short exactness means exactness in each degree.

source.place: CochainComplex.stupidTruncShortComplex_shortExact, lines 288–342; Stacks more-algebra.tex, Tag 0ATI, lemma-perfect-ring-classical-generator, stupid-truncation induction.

proof.text: Define the inclusion componentwise by the inclusions of the upper stupid-truncation submodules. Define the projection to the single-term complex by identity in degree c and zero elsewhere. These are chain maps since all degrees below c vanish. In degree c the sequence is 0→0→K^c→K^c→0. Above c it is 0→K^i→K^i→0→0, and below c every term is zero. Thus it is degreewise short exact, so it is short exact as a sequence of complexes. This is the existing proved source-library theorem; no Lean theorem is introduced.
